Many live near ore-processing facilities that resumed operations six years ago. 
Locals suspect nearby mining activity may be responsible, though the company – Dundee Precious Metals – says no link has been established and it is in compliance with regulations. 
A clinical pharmacologist warns that any level of lead in the blood is dangerous and can cause serious health problems. Bosnian authorities are conducting further tests on more than 300 children.

Al Jazeera's Arduana Pribinja reports from Vares, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Mass killings in the Sudanese city of el-Fasher bear the hallmarks of genocide. 
Those are the findings of an independent UN investigation, which has been looking into the city's violent takeover by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

Human rights experts say the RSF's violations meet at least three criteria for genocide.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
South Korea’s former President Yoon Suk Yeol has been found guilty of masterminding an insurrection over his short-lived imposition of martial law in 2024.
The Seoul Central District Court sentenced Yoon to life in prison after ruling that he was the leader of the December 3, 2024 insurrection.
It also convicted and sentenced several former military and police officials involved in enforcing Yoon’s martial law decree, including ex-Defence Minister Kim Yong Hyun, who received a 30-year jail term.
Yoon, 65, has maintained his innocence throughout his court appearances and is likely to appeal the verdict.
Prosecutors had sought the death penalty for Yoon who was impeached and removed from office over his declaration of martial law.

Al Jazeera’s Jack Barton joins us live from Seoul to discuss the latest developments.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The United States has issued new threats against Tehran after a second round of nuclear talks, as Iran and Russia announced joint naval drills in the Sea of Oman to deter any “unilateral action” in the region.
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said on Wednesday that “Iran would be very wise to make a deal” with US President Donald Trump, after indirect talks in the Swiss city of Geneva ended without a significant breakthrough.
Leavitt told reporters that while some progress was made on Tuesday, “we’re still very apart on some issues”.
Trump – who has deployed two US aircraft carriers and thousands of troops to the Gulf region – escalated his rhetoric on social media.
“Should Iran decide not to make a Deal,” the US may need to use an Indian Ocean airbase in the Chagos Islands, “in order to eradicate a potential attack by a highly unstable and dangerous Regime”, he wrote on his Truth Social platform.
A previous negotiating effort collapsed last year when Israel launched attac
title: US renews threat of military action as Iran, Russia announce naval drills

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
An avalanche at California's Lake Tahoe has killed at least eight skiers, with a ninth person missing and presumed dead. 
The group of 15, including four guides, was descending Castle Peak when a large sheet of snow broke loose despite an avalanche watch being in effect. 
Six people were rescued after sheltering overnight in treacherous conditions and using emergency beacons to call for help. 
It is the deadliest avalanche in the United States in more than 40 years.

Al Jazeera's Heidi Zhou-Castro reports.
